botsim.fix.cf.title: Cloudflare WAF: Skip rule for AI bots
botsim.fix.cf.instructions: Place the rule above your existing blocking rules; it should show up as 'Skip' in Security Events.
botsim.fix.nginx.title: nginx: exempt AI bots from the UA block and rate limit
botsim.fix.nginx.instructions: Make your existing 'deny'/'return 403' and limit_req rules conditional on these variables, then run `nginx -t && nginx -s reload`.
botsim.fix.apache.title: Apache / LiteSpeed (.htaccess) and ModSecurity exception
botsim.fix.apache.instructions: After the change run `apachectl configtest && apachectl graceful`.
botsim.fix.aws.title: AWS WAF: Allow rule for AI bots + Bot Control exception
botsim.fix.aws.instructions: Add the Allow rule to the Web ACL with the lowest priority value (0, evaluated first); switch the CategoryAI rule in Bot Control to Count.
botsim.fix.akamai.title: Akamai Bot Manager: allow AI bots
botsim.fix.akamai.instructions: Security Configurations → Bot Manager → Known Bots → set the action of the 'AI Crawlers' / 'Web Search Engine Bots' categories to Allow (or Monitor). If a custom rule is needed, use this User-Agent regex: ({alt}).
botsim.fix.imperva.title: Imperva: mark AI bots as 'Good bots'
botsim.fix.imperva.instructions: Website → Security → Bot Protection → add the relevant AI bots to the Good Bots list; in Client Classification remove the Block/CAPTCHA action for 'Search bots/AI'.
botsim.fix.vercel.title: Vercel Firewall: bypass AI bots
botsim.fix.vercel.instructions: Project → Firewall → Bot Management → set the 'AI Bots' rule to Log/Off; Custom Rule: User Agent matches ({alt}) → Bypass. Turn off Attack Challenge Mode if it is enabled.
botsim.fix.sucuri.title: Sucuri WAF: add AI bots to the allowlist
botsim.fix.sucuri.instructions: Firewall → Access Control → add these UA fragments to Allowlist User Agents: {list}.
botsim.fix.datadome.title: DataDome: allow rule for AI bots
botsim.fix.datadome.instructions: Dashboard → Custom Rules → 'User-Agent contains' ({list}) → Allow; or set the 'AI Agents' category to Allow in Bot Management.
botsim.fix.perimeterx.title: HUMAN (PerimeterX): add AI bots to the allowlist
botsim.fix.console.instructions: Apply it in the admin console and run the simulation again.
botsim.fix.ssr.title: Render the content on the server (SSR/SSG/prerender)
botsim.fix.ssr.instructions: Use SSR or static generation in Next.js/Nuxt/SvelteKit; for a plain React SPA use prerendering (e.g. Rendertron, prerender.io) or move to a framework.
botsim.fix.diet.title: Reduce the AI token load (DOM and embedded JSON)
botsim.fix.diet.instructions: Target: text tokens / HTML tokens ratio ≥ 10%, HTML < 500 KB.
botsim.fix.cf.where: Cloudflare → Security → WAF → Custom rules → Create rule (move it to the TOP of the list)
botsim.fix.cf.strict: Verified bots only (immune to UA spoofing, recommended strict version):
botsim.fix.cf.also1: Also: Security → Bots → "Block AI bots" = Off, "AI Labyrinth" = Off;
botsim.fix.cf.also2: AI Crawl Control → the relevant crawlers = Allow. (Bot Fight Mode on the free plan cannot be bypassed with Skip → turn it off.)
